title: Sunday Ticket
summary: Work out which four NFL games to put on the multiview, then watch every one of your players score on the same board.
body: Sunday Ticket answers one question: given every league you play in, which NFL games have the most of your players in them? It reads your rosters, works out where your starters actually are on a Sunday, and ranks the games so the four boxes on your multiview are the four worth having.

body.heading: Reading the board
items: Your matchup, up top. One card per league — your crest against your opponent's, both live scores, and how many starters each of you still has left to play. In both leagues, you get both cards.

Game boxes, below. One per NFL game in the window, ordered by how much of your roster is in it. Each player row shows his live fantasy points in that league's scoring, so the same player can carry two different numbers.
The Updated pill. When the board last actually heard from MFL. A board that says "live" and has not been confirmed since noon is not live, and the pill is how you tell.

body: The numbers refresh about once a minute while games are being played, then back off once everything is final. Lose your connection mid-afternoon and the scores you already have stay put rather than blanking out — a stale number with a timestamp on it beats a blank one.

body.heading: Two things it deliberately will not do
items: Leagues from outside this site show projections only. We can read your rosters there, but not their live scoring — those cards say Projections only rather than quietly showing you zeroes.
It is the wide shot, not the box score. For scoring plays, the ticker and the full breakdown, Live Scoring is still the deep cut.

body: Your country and clock preferences change what Sunday Ticket prints beside each game — kickoff times in your own clock, and the TV channel for where you actually live. Both are set on Preferences.
